title: Ezra Caudell, 19, receiving ‘multi-system trauma’ care after Philadelphia Cycling Classic crash
content:
Ezra Caudell remains in hospital and is receiving care for “multi-system trauma” after a crash during Sunday’s Philadelphia Cycling Classic.

The incident occurred after a collision with Lotto Intermarché rider Milan Menten early in the race, with Caudell knocked unconscious and both riders taken to hospital.

Caudell, 19, is one of America’s most promising young road prospects and rides for George Hincapie’s Modern Adventure Pro Cycling Team, who provided the update on his condition on Tuesday evening.

“Ezra remains hospitalized and is actively receiving care for multi-system trauma he sustained as a result of his crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic,” the team wrote.

“He has an incredible team working diligently and family at his bedside.  We are grateful for the thoughts and ongoing outpouring of support.”

Philadelphia mayor Cherelle L. Parker wrote after the race that: “We are also closely monitoring two cyclists from the men’s race who were injured and required treatment at local hospitals.

“City first responders, including our Fire Department, on-site medical personnel, and my leadership team responded immediately to the incident, and I am grateful for their service.

“My team and I are at the hospital now. Our thoughts and prayers are with both cyclists, their families and teams. Let’s lift them up as a city in prayer tonight.”

Caudell was the youngest rider to start the prestigious Paris-Roubaix this spring, where he finished 121st, while he also raced at the Arctic Race of Norway and Tour of Denmark this summer. He finished seventh in the road race at the men’s senior national championships this June.

Lotto Intermarché have not provided an update on Menten’s condition, which is not thought to be serious.

The Philadelphia Cycling Classic, one of America’s most prestigious one-day races, was resurrected this weekend after a 10 year hiatus. Lidl-Trek’s Tim Torn Teutenberg won the men’s race in a sprint, with Chiara Consonni taking the women’s title in a photo finish.
